title: The Fairness Lie Detector — three broken schedulers caught by name

source.source_reference: Shawn's explicit teaching, 2026-10-10. Ratified as law.

intelligence.essence: The fairness rules now have their own lie detector. Three deliberately broken schedulers — one that starves work quietly, one that starves flickering work, one that looks busy without accomplishing anything — were built, and the checker caught all three, each by its right name: WF_VIOLATION, SF_ONLY_VIOLATION, PROGRESS_ON_SERVICE_VIOLATION. Nine layers deep, 390 tests green. The checker never says 'all good' — it says precisely what was tested and what wasn't.

human_view.meaning: We built a machine that checks whether work is being treated fairly — and then we tried to fool it three different ways. It caught every trick and named each one correctly. It also never overclaims: instead of 'all good' it tells you exactly what it did and didn't test.
human_view.why_it_matters: This is the difference between a system that looks fair and a system proven fair. Shawn called it 'really good — good for our health, good for our intelligence.'

simple_view.meaning: We built a fairness checker, tried to trick it three ways, and it caught every trick by name.

naya_view.directive: When verifying any scheduler: test it against deliberately broken variants first. A verifier that cannot catch a known-broken scheduler cannot be trusted with an unknown one. Report verdicts as scoped statements, never blanket passes.

ai_view.specification: Discriminating suite: WF-01/WF-02 (weak fairness), SF-01/SF-02 (strong fairness), POS-01/02/03 (progress on service), 8/8 classifying correctly. Assumption-guarantee audit rejects circular assumptions. Vacuity detection rejects meaningless passes. Verdict vocabulary: OBSERVED_NO_VIOLATION_WITHIN_TESTED_TRACE, MODEL_CHECK_PASSED_IN_SCOPE, FAIRNESS_QUALIFIED_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS, WORKFLOW_COMPLETED_IN_SCOPE — never collapsed to one green PASS.
ai_view.directive: Reproduce this pattern for every future liveness/safety verifier: broken-variant self-test first.

machine_view.optimization_function: max(Verified_Human_Value / Time) subject to Proof, Provenance, Continuity
roadmap: wire verifier onto canonical PROVE seam
machine_view.optimization_target: Every verifier earns trust by catching known defects before claiming unknown correctness.

intelligence.learning_lesson: A verifier proves itself by catching deliberate defects, not by passing clean inputs. The broken-scheduler test is the cheapest high-signal check in verification.
intelligence.priority: Milestone. Pattern to replicate across all future verifiers.
decisions: Built 2026-10-10 from Naya 1's verification intel; commissioned by Shawn's live intel pipeline.

connections.target: SN-0881 — The Freshness Law (scoped verdicts honor it)

intelligence.uncertainty: 390-test / 9-layer figures are Shawn's reported integration-team state, not independently verified from this seat. The 8/8 discriminating suite is independently verified here.
intelligence.applicability: All future scheduler/liveness/safety verifiers across Team Naya.
intelligence.falsifier: Falsified if the verifier passes a deliberately broken scheduler variant, or issues a blanket PASS beyond its tested scope.
intelligence.measurement_contract: Broken-variant catch rate: 3/3 required. Discriminating suite: 8/8 required. Blanket PASS statements: zero tolerated.
intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor learns the rule: never trust a verifier that hasn't caught a known-broken variant first.
